gen-gf-bellota-text-gf-national-park: Bellota Text steps up with open, unshaded letters that look drawn with a single confident pen. National Park follows in a rounded plain sans, its pen never shifting pressure.
gen-gf-bellota-text-gf-noto-sans-cypriot: Noto Sans Cypriot has an e that opens up rather than closing its eye, friendly and easy to approach. Bellota Text above it is the showier of the two.
gen-gf-bellota-text-gf-noto-sans-cypro-m: Flat, stencil-like lines up top, then a quieter body below. Bellota Text is best at being noticed in display sizes, while Noto Sans Cypro Minoan is best at stepping back with its cut-back terminals and sans-serif manner.
gen-gf-bellota-text-gf-noto-sans-hatran: Approachable in spirit, Noto Sans Hatran has a wide funnel-like throat in its e, under Bellota Text's strings of steady strokes. Its sans-serif lines keep going smoothly.
gen-gf-bellota-text-gf-noto-sans-inscrip: Bellota Text draws monoline strokes with commanding, distinctive presence, and its open shapes stand out. Noto Sans Inscriptional Pahlavi then keeps every small counter unclogged, so the sans text stays easy to follow.
gen-gf-bellota-text-gf-noto-sans-javanes: Clean and tidy, Bellota Text carries no thick-thin pulse, just one distinctive, commanding line. Noto Sans Javanese backs that up with apertures keeping its counters connected to the space outside.
gen-gf-bellota-text-gf-noto-sans-kawi: Noto Sans Kawi has an open-jawed c like a pair of pliers, and its sans shapes stay quietly clean. Bellota Text, bent as if from one wire, takes the louder role.
gen-gf-bellota-text-gf-noto-sans-manicha: Bellota Text draws a constant-width line, like a marker, with commanding and distinctive character. And Noto Sans Manichaean, with crossbars that have open mouths, gives that heading a modern, clean partner.
gen-gf-bellota-text-gf-noto-sans-new-tai: Bellota Text lays fine rope-like strokes into commanding letter shapes, earning its keep big and short. Noto Sans New Tai Lue stays cupped and modern.
gen-gf-bellota-text-gf-noto-sans-old-sou: Rope-calm lettering, open and unshaded, is Bellota Text. Noto Sans Old South Arabian follows in a plain sans whose curved strokes end before turning inward, keeping the page approachable.
